newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's seen making regulation panel appointments.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's seen making regulation panel appointments.

text.p: Lloyd's of London is expected to announce shortly, possibly on Friday, the appointments of around a dozen senior figures, whose brief will be to report within six months on how the insurance market should be regulated.

The appointments will include people from outside Lloyd's, who have experience in senior positions of other regulated financial markets, as well as representatives of the managing agency community, corporate investors, and Names, who are the individuals who have traditionally backed the insurance market.
Industry sources said on Thursday that the terms of reference for the regulatory review, which has been gathering momentum since the summer, would also be detailed.
The review is part of a wide-ranging internal examination at Lloyd's of how the insurance market should proceed now that its recovery plan has succeeded.

Lloyd's in September declared unconditional a 3.2 billion stg settlement to the Names, compensating them for more than 8.0 billion stg in losses over five years from 1988 to 1992 on condition they help pay for reinsuring those losses into a new company called Equitas and drop litigation against Lloyd's.

Most of the market's previous headaches are behind it, but its significantly reduced legal problems took another twist on Thursday when a UK appeals court ruled that certain amendments in a recent case, which allowed Lloyd's to take legal winnings from Names, were unlawful. Lloyd's is considering the ruling.
Sir Alan Hardcastle, chairman of Lloyd's regulatory board, is to chair the review group, which is expected to encourage some degree of external regulation of the insurance market.
One possible scenario is that a regulator like the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) could take on certain responsibilities, altering the role of Lloyd's ruling council.
